question: Do explicitly declared input projections or existing independent predictors improve retrospective measured-cohort ordering over native RN.Ai?
provider: Pinned local backends under prior explicit local-fallback approval; no new remote jobs. Boltzmann siRNA contract inspected; it exposes no RN.Ai core-tokenization, RNAiSpline, batching or physical-dangle configuration controls.

config_order.purpose: Prior RN.Ai convention; explicit site/context audit added.
Input-length ablation: zero-pad guide tokens 20/21 rather than retaining source overhang tokens.
Alternate independent efficacy endpoint; never averaged with RN.Ai/OligoFormer.
Reuse full-pool native scores with coordinate/sequence identity checks; no fresh OligoFormer forward pass.

selection_protocol.primary_efficacy_metric: ROC AUC at observed label >=0.7; native endpoints kept separate
selection_protocol.selection: For each of three eligible target genes, choose among each prefix of frozen configs using mean AUC on the OTHER TWO genes; report selected config AUC on that gene. No ensemble or refit.
selection_protocol.exposure_warning: All these historical cohorts were examined previously. Retrospective leave-one-target-out is NOT an untouched prospective holdout.
selection_protocol.bootstrap: 1000 paired class-stratified row resamples for exploratory AUC/delta intervals; shared/overlapping sites violate row independence; no superiority claim. Small class counts <5 suppress intervals.
selection_protocol.TTR: Two fixed known drug-core anchors ranked among all 598 windows. No config is selected to optimize their rank. Clinical outcomes never treated as sequence labels.
selection_protocol.HTT: Thermodynamic dangle/noLP and missing-context sensitivity only. No new allele/CNS design or config promotion.
